content.title: Complete an existing task by clicking its checkbox
content.test_md_blob:
# Complete an existing task by clicking its checkbox

> Prove that clicking an existing incomplete task's checkbox marks that task complete and shows the completed presentation.

## Import: t-1

@import t-1

## Step 1

Open {{start_url}} in a browser and wait until the todo list page is fully loaded with the task created by the reused setup visible in the list.

## Step 2

Store the completion state of the task titled "Buy milk" as baseline_completion_state, confirming that its checkbox is not checked and its title is not shown with strikethrough styling before any action.

## Step 3

On the todo list page, in the row for the task titled "Buy milk", click its checkbox to mark that task complete.

## Step 4

Assert that the same task row is now shown as completed and that the task title is rendered with strikethrough styling.

## Step 5 — assert @verifies ac-3, ac-4

Confirm state-transition check: completed (equals) — the stated promise: Clicking an existing task's checkbox changes that task from not completed to completed.

judgements.rationale: [value_score] Kept this scenario-test pair because it is the only live scenario, covers the core promised interaction, and closes parity for the use-case within the budget ceiling.

[self_critique] Oracle proof: the formal check used a state-transition oracle tied to ac-3 and included a baseline-capture step before the checkbox action, so it proved the completion change rather than only observing the final UI.

[self_critique] Technique fit: reusing t-1 was appropriate because this use-case required an existing task and the imported web test creates one on the same surface without inventing external fixtures.
[self_critique] Negative coverage: no negative completion test was added because the PRD did not specify blocked completion, invalid checkbox states, or failure behavior for this use-case.

[self_critique] Assertion breadth: the visible post-action assertion was limited to the same task row titled "Buy milk" so the test did not over-claim that every task or every style on the page changed.
